## 1. Process Hollowing & Cobalt Strike Beacon Loader
- **Scenario ID:** `process-hollowing`
- **Code:** T1055.012
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/process-hollowing
- **Category:** Malware & Process Execution (`MALWARE`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1106 (Native API: CreateProcessW), T1055.012 (Process Injection: Process Hollowing), T1055.012 (Process Hollowing: Memory Write), T1055.012 (Thread Context Hijacking & Execution), T1071.001 (Application Layer Protocol: Web C2)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2023-36884 (8.8 HIGH), CVE-2024-21412 (8.1 HIGH)
- **Attributed Threat Actors:** APT29 (Midnight Blizzard), TA551 (Shathak) & QakBot Affiliates
- **Executive Summary:** Imagine an intruder who wants to enter a high-security bank without raising an alarm. Instead of breaking down the front door in a ski mask, they hire an official armored bank truck, freeze it inside the garage before the driver even starts the route, and pocket two golden master keys: the first master key unlocks the rear cargo doors so they can empty all the legal bank gold and load their own covert crew inside, and the second master key unlocks the driver cab so they can reprogram the GPS route and release the brake. When the truck rolls out, every security camera and guard at the gate still sees the bank’s own trusted license plate and uniform. In this scenario (T1055.012, Process Hollowing & Cobalt Strike Beacon Loader) on WKS-04 (10.10.4), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: launching a Legitimate Windows Process, then hollowing Out the Original svchost.exe Code, then allocating Writable-Executable Memory, then hijacking the CPU Thread Context. Steps #1–#5 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Launching a Legitimate Windows Process, then Hollowing Out the Original svchost.exe Code, then Allocating Writable-Executable Memory, then Hijacking the CPU Thread Context, then Outbound HTTPS Command-and-Control Beacon. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (5):**
  1. **[T1106] CREATE SUSPENDED TARGET PROCESS** (Native API: CreateProcessW): Instead of kicking down the bank’s front door in a ski mask, the intruder walks up to the dispatch desk and hires an official armored bank truck. The split-second the truck rolls into the private garage bay, before the driver even turns the ignition, the intruder slams a freeze switch that locks the entire truck in ice-blue stillness and pockets two golden master keys: the first master key unlocks the rear cargo bay so the intruder can empty the bank gold and load their covert crew, and the second master key unlocks the driver cab and ignition so they can later change the GPS route and release the brake. The attacker’s goal on Victim Laptop WKS-04 (10.10.4.15) is to run Beacon without triggering antivirus or application-allowlisting rules that would block an unknown new .exe on disk. Acting as the intruder at the dispatch desk, the initial loader (Invoice_Q4.exe, PID 3104, the stage-1 file executed on that host) calls CreateProcessW (Windows’ standard user-mode API for launching a new program) to hire our "official armored bank truck", a real Windows system binary: C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe (PID 4892, chosen because svchost.exe carries a valid Microsoft digital signature, so security tools and analysts naturally expect to see it running in the background). Hitting the "garage freeze switch" means passing the creation flag CREATE_SUSPENDED = 0x00000004 (which instructs the Windows kernel to assemble the process container in RAM and create its main worker thread TID 4896, but pause it at the starting line before its first line of code can execute). In response, the Windows kernel hands back a populated PROCESS_INFORMATION structure (Windows’ startup receipt) containing the "two golden master keys": Process Master Key hProcess = 0x01C4 (a numeric permission handle that unlocks svchost.exe’s virtual memory so Invoice_Q4.exe can inspect, erase, and inject code into it during Steps #2 and #3) and Thread Master Key hThread = 0x01C8 (a separate permission handle that unlocks the paused thread’s CPU controls so Invoice_Q4.exe can redirect its starting address and wake it up in Step #4). When CreateProcessW (Windows’ user-mode function for starting a program) is invoked with CREATE_SUSPENDED (0x00000004, a creation flag that pauses the new program before its first instruction runs so the attacker gets a quiet window to swap its contents), it calls ntdll!NtCreateUserProcess (the low-level system call inside ntdll.dll that crosses into the Windows kernel to build a new process). Inside the kernel, Windows allocates an EPROCESS object for PID 4892 (the kernel’s master tracking record storing the process’s trusted svchost.exe identity, security token, and memory map), maps ntdll.dll (Windows’ mandatory core bridge library required by every process to make kernel requests) and the signed svchost.exe binary at base address 0x00400000 (the standard starting memory slot where Windows loads executable code so internal memory jumps line up cleanly), and parks the primary thread TID 4896 (the main execution worker assigned to run the program’s CPU instructions) at ntdll!RtlUserThreadStart (Windows’ built-in thread launchpad where every new thread waits right before jumping into the program’s own startup code) with SuspendCount = 1 (a kernel pause counter set to 1 so the CPU scheduler skips this thread and keeps the child process completely inert in RAM until resumed). At the same time, Windows grants the parent dropper PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS = 0x1FFFFF (the highest possible Windows permission mask allowing full memory reading, unmapping, writing, and thread manipulation) through two returned master key handles: hProcess = 0x01C4 (the Process Master Key used to modify svchost.exe’s RAM in Steps #2 and #3) and hThread = 0x01C8 (the Thread Master Key used to redirect CPU registers and unfreeze TID 4896 in Step #4). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ CREATE_SUSPENDED / ⇠#1 ACK PID 4892) from Node ① (#1 Attacker Phishing & C2 Server) to Node ② (#2 Edge Firewall & Mail GW), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & Sysmon EDR Sensor).
  2. **[T1055.012] UNMAP LEGITIMATE MEMORY IMAGE** (Process Injection: Process Hollowing): Using the first golden master key (the cargo-door key from Step #1) while the official armored bank truck stays frozen inside the garage, an overhead X-ray gantry scans the truck’s cargo manifest to pinpoint where every gold bar is stored. The heavy rear blast doors swing wide open and every crate of genuine bank bullion slides out onto the unloading ramp and vanishes, leaving a completely hollow truck inside while its official bank paint and license plate stay untouched outside. Now that the "frozen armored bank truck", svchost.exe (PID 4892, still halted in memory so it cannot run or trigger normal runtime checks), is parked inside the bay, Invoice_Q4.exe (PID 3104) uses its first golden master key, Process Master Key hProcess = 0x01C4 (the memory-access permission handle obtained in Step #1 specifically for reading and editing the child’s RAM), to scan the truck’s "cargo manifest": the child’s Process Environment Block (PEB, Windows’ internal summary table storing a process’s loaded modules and memory layout, read at offset PEB+0x10 so the loader learns the exact starting address where svchost.exe was mapped: ImageBaseAddress = 0x00400000). Emptying out every "crate of genuine bank bullion" happens when the loader calls ntdll!NtUnmapViewOfSection(hProcess = 0x01C4, BaseAddr = 0x00400000) (a low-level native Windows syscall that detaches and removes the original Microsoft svchost.exe code from RAM without terminating the process), and the kernel replies with NTSTATUS = 0x00000000 (STATUS_SUCCESS, the kernel confirmation code proving that memory slot 0x00400000 inside PID 4892 is now completely hollow and ready for the covert crew). When NtUnmapViewOfSection (the user-mode native API wrapper in ntdll.dll used to detach a mapped memory section) transitions into kernel routine nt!MiUnmapViewOfSection (the internal Windows kernel function that tears down mapped views of an executable file), the Windows Virtual Memory Manager (the OS subsystem that tracks which memory pages belong to each process) removes the file-backed SEC_IMAGE mapping (a special kernel memory region tied directly to a signed executable file on disk) from the process’s Virtual Address Descriptor (VAD, the kernel’s internal tree inventory recording every allocated address range and its read/write/execute permissions) for C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe at 0x00400000 and returns STATUS_SUCCESS = 0x00000000 (freeing the exact 0x00400000 base address so the replacement malware image can be loaded there in Step #3 without needing complex internal pointer relocations, while PID 4892 still retains its Microsoft-signed process name and token in the kernel process table). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ NtUnmapView / ⇠#2 RET 0x00400000) from Node ② (#2 Edge Firewall & Mail GW) to Node ③ (#3 Victim Laptop (WKS-04)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & Sysmon EDR Sensor).
  3. **[T1055.012] ALLOCATE RWX & WRITE MALICIOUS PE** (Process Hollowing: Memory Write): Keeping the rear cargo bay open with that same cargo-door master key, the intruder unlocks a hidden high-clearance compartment inside the empty armored bank truck with all security barriers disabled, then quietly marches their covert crew and mission crate straight up the rear ramp into the hollow bay. The blast doors swing shut around the trusted exterior paint and license plate so nobody outside notices the swap. Carving out that "unlocked secret cargo bay" at the exact vacated slot (0x00400000, reusing the original base address freed in Step #2 so internal code pointers inside the malware do not break), Invoice_Q4.exe (PID 3104) again uses Process Master Key hProcess = 0x01C4 (holding GrantedAccess = 0x1FFFFF, the full permission mask allowing cross-process memory allocation and writing) to call VirtualAllocEx (Windows’ cross-process memory reservation API) and reserve 264 KB (270,336 bytes) of private memory with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE = 0x40 permissions (known as RWX, allowing the loader to write payload bytes into that memory right now and letting the CPU immediately execute those same bytes as code a moment later). Marching the "covert crew and mission crate" up the rear ramp is WriteProcessMemory (Windows’ API for copying bytes from one process into another process’s RAM) streaming the unpacked Cobalt Strike Beacon PE headers ("MZ" / 4D 5A, the two-byte magic signature identifying every Windows executable) and its core program sections (.text for executable instructions.rdata for read-only constants and import tables, and .data for writable variables) directly into svchost.exe’s RAM, returning lpNumberOfBytesWritten = 270,336 (confirming the entire covert payload and its startup entry point at 0x004014A0 are sealed inside the trusted truck without ever writing a malware file to the hard drive). Across the kernel syscall pair NtAllocateVirtualMemory (the low-level kernel routine that reserves and commits new virtual memory pages inside a target process) and NtWriteVirtualMemory (the kernel routine that copies raw bytes across process boundaries), Windows creates an unbacked private memory region marked MEM_PRIVATE (anonymous RAM not tied to any signed file on disk) with PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE = 0x40 permissions at 0x00400000 (which immediately stands out forensically because a legitimate program loaded from disk uses file-backed SEC_IMAGE pages that strictly separate Read-Execute code in .text = 0x20 from Read-Write data in .data = 0x04 so code cannot be rewritten on the fly). Committing 270,336 bytes containing an "MZ" PE header (4D 5A, the unmistakable fingerprint of a full Windows executable) into unbacked RWX memory inside svchost.exe (PID 4892) is one of the strongest forensic indicators of process hollowing. On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ RWX WRITE / ⇠#3 ACK 264 KB) from Node ③ (#3 Victim Laptop (WKS-04)) to Node ④ (#4 Invoice_Q4.exe → svchost.exe), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & Sysmon EDR Sensor).
  4. **[T1055.012] PATCH THREAD CONTEXT & RESUME** (Thread Context Hijacking & Execution): With the covert crew sealed in the back, the intruder now pulls out the second golden master key (the cab-and-ignition key from Step #1) to unlock the frozen truck’s front cab before releasing the brake. They turn the steering wheel hard, erase the bank’s official route from the dashboard GPS, dial in their own secret destination, and finally shatter the freeze lock, releasing the handbrake so the official bank truck roars out of the garage onto the intruder’s route. Even though the "covert crew" (Cobalt Strike Beacon) is now sealed inside svchost.exe (PID 4892 at 0x00400000), the frozen driver thread (TID 4896, controlled via the second golden master key, Thread Master Key hThread = 0x01C8 obtained in Step #1 specifically for steering and waking the paused thread) is still aimed at the old Microsoft startup route. Reprogramming the "dashboard GPS and steering wheel" means Invoice_Q4.exe (PID 3104) calls SetThreadContext(hThread = 0x01C8) (Windows’ API for rewriting a paused thread’s saved CPU registers) to overwrite the thread’s RCX register (on 64-bit Windows, a brand-new suspended thread holds its upcoming program startup address inside CPU register RCX, so changing RCX aims the thread straight at the injected Beacon without calling noisier APIs like CreateRemoteThread) with 0x004014A0 (calculated as Base 0x00400000 plus EntryPoint RVA 0x14A0, the byte offset to the Beacon’s first executable instruction). Finally, "shattering the freeze lock and releasing the brake" is ResumeThread(hThread = 0x01C8) (Windows’ API that lowers a thread’s pause counter from 1 down to 0, returning PreviousSuspendCount = 1 to confirm the thread was previously paused and launching TID 4896 so the hijacked truck immediately runs the Beacon). When NtSetContextThread (the kernel syscall that modifies a suspended thread’s saved CPU register state) and NtResumeThread (the kernel syscall that decrements a thread’s pause counter so the CPU scheduler can dispatch it) complete in the kernel, Windows updates the thread’s saved trap frame at KTRAP_FRAME.Rcx = 0x004014A0 (the kernel memory snapshot holding the CPU register values that will be loaded onto the processor the instant this thread wakes up) and releases TID 4896 from ntdll!RtlUserThreadStart (Windows’ thread startup launchpad, which immediately jumps execution to whatever address sits in RCX) into active user-mode execution. Because TID 4896 is now running independently inside svchost.exe (PID 4892), the original stage-1 loader Invoice_Q4.exe (PID 3104) can safely exit while the Beacon survives inside the trusted system process, although waking the tampered thread simultaneously fires kernel image-tampering callbacks (alerting Sysmon EventID 25 because the live executable pages at 0x00400000 no longer match the signed svchost.exe file on disk). On the diagram, follow Step #4 / Link #4 (#4→ IMAGE TAMPERED / ⇠#4 ACK EID 25) from Node ④ (#4 Invoice_Q4.exe → svchost.exe) to Node ⑤ (#5 Corp DC01 & Internal Shares), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & Sysmon EDR Sensor).
  5. **[T1071.001] OUTBOUND C2 BEACON OVER HTTPS** (Application Layer Protocol: Web C2): Now rolling down the boulevard, the disguised armored bank truck pulls up to the high-security checkpoint gate. The security cameras read the bank’s official license plate, the uniformed guard smiles and lifts the barrier, and the truck opens a hidden encrypted courier line straight to the intruder’s remote warehouse, until a watchful control-room radar notices the truck drove out on an unscheduled route without a dispatch slip. Rolling past the "checkpoint guard" in the bank’s own trusted uniform means the Beacon is executing inside C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe (PID 4892, so path-based endpoint firewall rules see a trusted Windows binary requesting network access and automatically allow the connection). Opening the "hidden encrypted courier line to the secret warehouse" is Cobalt Strike loading winhttp.dll (Windows’ built-in HTTP client library, used so the implant relies on legitimate OS networking code), establishing a TLS 1.3 HTTPS connection (modern transport encryption that hides commands from basic packet inspection) over TCP port 443 (the standard HTTPS web port chosen to blend in with normal employee browsing) to the external Command-and-Control server at 185.220.101.42:443, and sending an HTTP GET request for /jquery-3.3.1.min.js (a Malleable C2 disguise profile that hides RSA-encrypted victim host metadata inside the HTTP Cookie header to mimic a harmless web script download). The remote warehouse (185.220.101.42:443) replies with HTTP 200 OK (disguised as an application/javascript file carrying AES-encrypted operator tasking and a 60-second callback interval with 20% random jitter, intentionally varying check-in timing to evade simple fixed-timer beacon detectors). Application-based host firewalls often permit C:\Windows\System32\svchost.exe (trusted by file path as a core Windows service host binary) to initiate outbound HTTPS connections through the perimeter NAT (Network Address Translation gateway forwarding corporate workstation traffic to the internet). However, a genuine svchost.exe is always spawned by services.exe (Windows’ official Service Control Manager) and always carries a "-k <ServiceGroup>" command-line flag (which tells Windows which bundle of system services that host process should run), so a bare svchost.exe (PID 4892) spawned by Invoice_Q4.exe (PID 3104) negotiating TLS 1.3 with JA3 fingerprint 72a589da586844d7f0818ce684948eea (a hash of the client’s TLS handshake parameters that fingerprints Cobalt Strike’s network stack even when payloads are encrypted) and polling /jquery-3.3.1.min.js every 60s (±20% jitter) is immediately caught by SIEM correlation. On the diagram, follow Step #5 / Link #5 (#5→ C2 BEACON / ⇠#5 RESP 1.4 KB) from Node ⑤ (#5 Corp DC01 & Internal Shares) to Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & Sysmon EDR Sensor), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 SOC SIEM & Sysmon EDR Sensor).
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Microsoft Win32 API Reference — *CreateProcessW (CREATE_SUSPENDED), VirtualAllocEx & WriteProcessMemory* (`MSDN-WIN32-MEMORY`): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-createprocessw
  - Microsoft Sysinternals — *Sysmon Event ID 25: ProcessTampering (Image is replaced)* (`SYSMON-EID-25`): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon#event-id-25-processtampering
  - Elastic Security Labs — *Hunting Memory Injection & Process Tampering via Kernel ETW Threat Intelligence* (`ELASTIC-MEM-ETW`): https://www.elastic.co/security-labs

## 2. Fileless AMSI Memory Bypass & Reflective DLL Injection
- **Scenario ID:** `amsi-reflective-dll`
- **Code:** T1562.001 / T1620
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/amsi-reflective-dll
- **Category:** Malware & Process Execution (`MALWARE`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1059.001 (Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell), T1562.001 (Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools), T1562.001 (Impair Defenses: AMSI Memory Patching), T1620 (Reflective Code Loading)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2023-23397, CVE-2024-21351
- **Executive Summary:** Hidden PowerShell (`PID 5412`) spawned by `winword.exe` (`PID 3820`) on `WKS-FIN-09` resolves `amsi.dll!AmsiScanBuffer` (`0x7FF9C2142840`) inside its own Ring 3 address space, unlocks the signed code page with `VirtualProtect` (`0x20 -> 0x40`), overwrites its opening six bytes with `B8 57 00 07 80 C3` (`mov eax, 0x80070057; ret` = `E_INVALIDARG`) before restoring `0x20 RX`, and then streams a 184 KB reflective payload from `198.51.100.74:443` straight into unbacked `MEM_PRIVATE RWX` RAM (`0x000001E4A2100000`) with zero bytes written to NTFS. Defenders catch the chain through PowerShell Operational Event ID 4104, Kernel `EtwTiLogProtectVM`, Sysmon Event ID 3, and `.NET` Runtime ETW Event ID 152.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1059.001] ENCODED POWERSHELL STAGER & AMSI ADDRESS LOOKUP**: `winword.exe` spawns hidden encoded `powershell.exe` resolving `amsi.dll!AmsiScanBuffer` (`0x7FF9C2142840`) while PowerShell Operational EID 4104 captures the plaintext script block pre-bypass.
  2. **[T1562.001] VIRTUALPROTECT MEMORY GUARD UNLOCK (RX -> RWX)**: `VirtualProtect(0x7FF9C2142840, 6, 0x40, &old)` triggers Copy-on-Write inside PID 5412 and emits Ring 0 `EtwTiLogProtectVM`.
  3. **[T1562.001] 6-BYTE PROLOGUE SHORT-CIRCUIT PATCH & RE-LOCK**: `Marshal.Copy` replaces `4C 8B DC 49 89 5B` with `B8 57 00 07 80 C3` (`E_INVALIDARG`), silencing Defender (`MpOav.dll`), then restores `PAGE_EXECUTE_READ (0x20)`.
  4. **[T1620] ZERO-DISK DOWNLOAD & IN-MEMORY REFLECTIVE LOAD**: `WebClient.DownloadData` + `[System.Reflection.Assembly]::Load($bytes)` maps an unbacked `MEM_PRIVATE RWX` PE at `0x000001E4A2100000` (0 NTFS bytes, zero Sysmon EID 11), correlated via Sysmon EID 3 and `.NET` ETW EID 152.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Microsoft Learn — *Antimalware Scan Interface (AMSI) Developer Architecture* (`MS-AMSI-ARCH`): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/amsi/antimalware-scan-interface-portal
  - Microsoft PowerShell Team — *PowerShell Operational Log Event ID 4104 (Script Block Logging)* (`MS-PS-EID-4104`): https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_logging_windows
  - The MITRE Corporation & Defender Threat Intelligence — *MITRE ATT&CK T1620 & T1562.001: Reflective Code Loading & AMSI Memory Patching* (`ATT&CK-T1620-T1562`): https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1620/

## 3. LockBit 3.0 Ransomware Behavioral Analysis: VSS Wipe & Fast IOCP Encryption
- **Scenario ID:** `ransomware-shadow-wipe`
- **Code:** T1486 / T1490
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/ransomware-shadow-wipe
- **Category:** Ransomware & Extortion (`RANSOMWARE_EXTORTION`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1569.002 (System Services: Service Execution), T1490 (Inhibit System Recovery), T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact), T1070.001 (Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CISA AA23-165A (Understanding Ransomware Threat Actors: LockBit), CVE-2023-4966
- **Executive Summary:** Compromised Domain Admin credentials on `JUMP-OPS-02` (`10.10.15.8`) push `lb3_black.exe` over SMB `ADMIN$` (`WinSec EID 5145`) and register `PSEXESVC` (`System EID 7045`) as `NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM` on `FS-CORP-01` (`10.10.50.14`) to launch `lb3_black.exe -pass 8f91c2a0` (`PID 6412`). The locker wipes Volume Shadow Copies (`vssadmin`, `wmic`, `bcdedit`) and halts `VSS`/`sqlservr`/`VeeamBackupSvc` (`EID 7036`), encrypts the opening `4 KB–64 KB` header of `4,820` files across `D:\Finance_Shares\`, `D:\HR_Records\`, and `D:\CAD_Archives\` in `11.4s` via 8-thread asynchronous IOCP `ChaCha20 + RSA-2048` (`*.lockbit`), drops `Restore-My-Files.txt` + `lb3_wall.bmp`, and executes `wevtutil.exe cl Security` (`PID 6618`, `WinSec EID 1102`) while off-host SIEM preserves the complete attack timeline.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1569.002] LATERAL PSEXEC STAGING & SYSTEM SERVICE CREATION**: `JUMP-OPS-02` copies `lb3_black.exe` to `ADMIN$` (`EID 5145`) and starts `PSEXESVC` (`EID 7045`) to launch password-gated `lb3_black.exe -pass 8f91c2a0` (`PID 6412`).
  2. **[T1490] SHADOW COPY PURGE & BACKUP SERVICE TERMINATION**: `vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet` (`PID 6504`), `wmic shadowcopy delete`, `bcdedit.exe` recovery lockout (`PID 6540`), and stopping `VSS`/`sqlservr`/`VeeamBackupSvc` (`EID 7036`).
  3. **[T1486] HIGH-SPEED IOCP INTERMITTENT ENCRYPTION**: 8-thread `CreateIoCompletionPort` workers seal the opening `4 KB–64 KB` header of `4,820` files in `11.4s` with `ChaCha20` + `RSA-2048` and append `.lockbit` while excluding `C:\Windows`.
  4. **[T1070.001] RANSOM NOTE DROP & SECURITY EVENT LOG WIPE**: `Restore-My-Files.txt` drops across shares (`Sysmon EID 11`), `lb3_wall.bmp` replaces the desktop wallpaper (`Sysmon EID 13`), and `wevtutil.exe cl Security` (`PID 6618`) stamps `WinSec EID 1102` while off-host SIEM retains every earlier alert.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - CISA / FBI / MS-ISAC Joint Advisory — *Understanding Ransomware Threat Actors: LockBit (AA23-165A)*: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa23-165a
  - MITRE ATT&CK — *T1490 Inhibit System Recovery & T1486 Data Encrypted for Impact*: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
  - Microsoft Security — *Windows Security Event ID 1102 & System Event ID 7045 Auditing Reference*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-1102

## 4. Lazarus (SmoothOperator): 3CXDesktopApp Supply-Chain Compromise & Gopuram
- **Scenario ID:** `3cx-desktopapp-supply-chain-lazarus`
- **Code:** CVE-2023-29059
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/3cx-desktopapp-supply-chain-lazarus
- **Category:** Supply Chain & CI/CD (`SUPPLY_CHAIN_CICD`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1195.002 (Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain), T1574.002 (Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Side-Loading), T1102.001 (Web Service: Dead Drop Resolver), T1555.003 (Credentials from Web Browsers)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2023-29059 (CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL)
- **Executive Summary:** Pivoting from a prior trojanized Trading Technologies `X_TRADER` binary, Lazarus (`UNC4736` / `Labyrinth Chollima`) tampered with the 3CX CI/CD build server to swap `ffmpeg.dll` (unsigned sideload proxy) and `d3dcompiler_47.dll` (`0xFEEDFACE` + 312 KB RC4 payload) prior to genuine 3CX Ltd EV Authenticode signing (`v18.12.407`). On trading workstation `WKS-TRD-14` (`10.10.8.41`), signed `3CXDesktopApp.exe` (`PID 7120`) sideloads `ffmpeg.dll`, decrypts the payload with RC4 key `3jB(2bsG#@c7` into unbacked `MEM_PRIVATE RWX` RAM (`0x000001C948200000`), sleeps ~7 days before fetching GitHub `IconStorages/images/main/icon12.ico` trailing Base64 past EOF to contact `akamaitechcloudservices[.]com`, and executes `ICONICSTEALER` (`0x000001C948280000`) plus selective `Gopuram` backdoor deployment—exposed by `Sysmon EID 7/22/3` and behavioral EDR alerts on a VoIP binary reading Chrome/Edge `Login Data`.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1195.002] CASCADING X_TRADER PIVOT & PRE-SIGNING CI/CD SWAP**: `ffmpeg.dll` and `d3dcompiler_47.dll` swapped before valid 3CX EV Authenticode signing (`3CXDesktopApp-18.12.407.msi`); `Sysmon EID 7` catches unsigned child DLL loading.
  2. **[T1574.002] DLL SIDELOAD, 0xFEEDFACE MARKER & RC4 UNBACKED RWX**: `ffmpeg.dll` parses `0xFEEDFACE` in `d3dcompiler_47.dll` (`0x7FF8A1000000`) and RC4-decrypts (`3jB(2bsG#@c7`) 312 KB shellcode into `MEM_PRIVATE RWX` (`0x000001C948200000`).
  3. **[T1102.001] GITHUB ICONSTORAGES .ICO DEAD-DROP RESOLVER**: After dormancy, `PID 7120` fetches `raw.githubusercontent.com/IconStorages/images/main/icon12.ico` (`Sysmon EID 22/3`) and extracts trailing Base64 past EOF pointing to `akamaitechcloudservices[.]com`.
  4. **[T1555.003] ICONICSTEALER, SELECTIVE GOPURAM & BEHAVIORAL EDR**: `ICONICSTEALER` (`0x000001C948280000`) reads Chrome/Edge `Login Data` and hands high-value finance/crypto victims to `Gopuram`, triggering CrowdStrike Falcon behavioral alerts.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - CrowdStrike Intelligence — *3CXDesktopApp Supply Chain Compromise (Labyrinth Chollima / SmoothOperator)*: https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/crowdstrike-detects-and-prevents-active-intrusion-campaign-targeting-3cxdesktopapp-customers/
  - Mandiant — *3CX Software Supply Chain Compromise Initiated by a Prior Software Supply Chain Compromise (UNC4736 / X_TRADER)*: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/3cx-software-supply-chain-compromise
  - Kaspersky GReAT — *Gopuram Backdoor Deployed Through 3CX Supply Chain Attack*: https://securelist.com/gopuram-backdoor-deployed-through-3cx-supply-chain-attack/109344/

## 5. Andres Freund, Red Hat & Kaspersky — XZ Utils (liblzma) IFUNC sshd Supply Chain Backdoor
- **Scenario ID:** `xz-utils-cve-2024-3094-backdoor`
- **Code:** CVE-2024-3094
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/xz-utils-cve-2024-3094-backdoor
- **Category:** Malware & Process Execution (`MALWARE`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1195.002 (Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain), T1574.006 (Hijack Execution Flow: Dynamic Linker Hijacking), T1556 (Modify Authentication Process)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2024-3094 (CVSS 10.0 CRITICAL)
- **Executive Summary:** Maintainer persona Jia Tan embedded an obfuscated x86_64 object (`liblzma_la-crc64-fast.o`) inside binary unit-test fixture `tests/files/bad-3-corrupt_lzma2.xz` and shipped a release-tarball-only `m4/build-to-host.m4` script absent from upstream Git to compile the implant into `liblzma.so.5.6.1` during Debian/RPM packaging. When `/usr/sbin/sshd` starts on distro-patched Linux hosts, `libsystemd.so.0` transitively pulls `liblzma.so.5.6.1` into memory where GNU IFUNC resolver `crc64_resolve` (`0x7F9A21402000`) hooks `_dl_audit_preinit` and rewrites sshd `.got.plt` slot `0x55B2C4198048` (`RSA_public_decrypt`) from OpenSSL `libcrypto.so.3` (`0x7F9A20E14200`) to `liblzma.so.5.6.1` (`0x7F9A2143A110`) before Full RELRO locks the table read-only. Attacker-crafted RSA certificates carrying an `Ed448`-signed `ChaCha20` command trigger pre-auth root `system()` execution (`auditd SYSCALL 59`), until Andres Freund's `+508 ms` `perf record` / Valgrind discovery (`299 ms -> 807 ms`) stops CVE-2024-3094 prior to stable distro GA.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1195.002] UPSTREAM TARBALL SUBVERSION & M4/BUILD-TO-HOST.M4 TEST-FIXTURE EXTRACTION**: Tarball-only `m4/build-to-host.m4` decodes `tests/files/bad-3-corrupt_lzma2.xz` into `liblzma_la-crc64-fast.o` during x86_64 `.deb`/`.rpm` packaging.
  2. **[T1574.006] TRANSITIVE LIBSYSTEMD LINKAGE & GNU IFUNC PRE-RELRO GOT/PLT HIJACK**: `sshd -> libsystemd.so.0 -> liblzma.so.5.6.1` triggers `crc64_resolve` pre-main, rewriting `.got.plt` `0x55B2C4198048` (`RSA_public_decrypt`) before RELRO seals it read-only.
  3. **[T1556] PRE-AUTH RSA_PUBLIC_DECRYPT INTERCEPTION & ED448 ROOT COMMAND EXECUTION**: Normal SSH keys forward cleanly to `libcrypto.so.3`, while attacker `Ed448`-verified `ChaCha20` commands execute `system()` as `uid=0` caught by `auditd SYSCALL 59`.
  4. **[T1556] 500 MS CPU LATENCY ANOMALY (PERF) & FORENSIC SUPPLY-CHAIN DISCOVERY**: `+508 ms` SSH login delay (`299 ms -> 807 ms`) traced by `perf record` and Valgrind into `liblzma.so.5.6.1` leads to emergency downgrade to `xz-utils 5.4.5/5.4.6`.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Andres Freund (`oss-security`) — *Backdoor in upstream xz/liblzma leading to ssh server compromise (CVE-2024-3094)*: https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2024/03/29/4
  - Kaspersky GReAT (`Securelist`) — *XZ Utils Backdoor (CVE-2024-3094) Technical Analysis*: https://securelist.com/xz-backdoor-story-part-1/112354/
  - Red Hat & CISA — *Urgent Security Alert: CVE-2024-3094 (XZ Utils 5.6.0 / 5.6.1)*: https://www.redhat.com/en/blog/urgent-security-alert-fedora-41-and-rawhide-users

## 6. Microsoft Sysinternals & Splunk SURGe DFIR — LSASS MiniDump via comsvcs.dll & Sysmon EventID 10
- **Scenario ID:** `dfir-lsass-minidump-comsvcs-sysmon-eid10`
- **Code:** T1003.001
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/dfir-lsass-minidump-comsvcs-sysmon-eid10
- **Category:** Malware & Process Execution (`MALWARE`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1134 (Access Token Manipulation / SeDebugPrivilege), T1218.011 (System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32), T1003.001 (OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory)
- **Executive Summary:** On `WKS-ADM-07.corp.local` (`10.20.14.37`), an elevated session under `CORP\adm_jchen` holding `SeDebugPrivilege` (`Security EID 4672`) runs `tasklist /fi "imagename eq lsass.exe"` from `cmd.exe` (`PID 4920`) to resolve unprotected `lsass.exe` (`PID 684`, `RunAsPPL = 0`). Avoiding third-party tools, the operator launches signed `rundll32.exe` (`PID 5412`) with `C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, #24 684 C:\Windows\Temp\debug.dmp full`, acquiring `OpenProcess(0x1010)` (`PROCESS_VM_READ | PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION`) and serializing `lsasrv.dll!LogonSessionList` (`0x00007FF7A8100000`) and `msv1_0.dll`/`kerberos.dll` (`0x00007FFAD4200000`) via `dbgcore.dll!MiniDumpWriteDump(0x2)` into a `48.2 MB` `MDMP` (`4D 44 4D 50 93 A7`) file for offline `pypykatz` extraction. Defenders catch every variant via Sysmon `EID 10` (`GrantedAccess=0x1010`, `CallTrace` containing `comsvcs.dll` and `dbgcore.dll`), Sysmon `EID 11` + YARA, and prevent it outright with `RunAsPPL = 1` (`PsProtectedSignerLsa-Light`) and VBS Credential Guard (`LsaIso.exe`).
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1134] SEDEBUGPRIVILEGE ASSIGNMENT & LSASS.EXE PID 684 LOOKUP**: Elevated `CORP\adm_jchen` token (`Security EID 4672`) enumerates unprotected `lsass.exe` (`PID 684`, child of `services.exe` `PID 620`).
  2. **[T1218.011] SIGNED RUNDLL32 PROXY & COMSVCS.DLL ORDINAL #24 OPENPROCESS(0x1010)**: `rundll32.exe` (`PID 5412`) invokes `comsvcs.dll!MiniDump` (ordinal `#24`) opening handle `0x1010` to `lsass.exe`, captured in `Sysmon EID 10` `CallTrace`.
  3. **[T1003.001] DBGCORE.DLL MINIDUMPWRITEDUMP FULL-MEMORY SNAPSHOT (MDMP)**: `MiniDumpWriteDump(0x2)` dumps `48.2 MB` (`4D 44 4D 50 93 A7`) to `C:\Windows\Temp\debug.dmp` (`Sysmon EID 11`).
  4. **[T1003.001] OFFLINE PYPYKATZ EXTRACTION RISK, SIEM CORRELATION & RUNASPPL HARDENING**: Triple SIEM correlation (`EID 1 + 10 + 11`) triggers containment, credential rotation, and `RunAsPPL = 1` + Credential Guard (`LsaIso.exe`) deployment.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Microsoft Sysinternals — *Sysmon Event ID 10: ProcessAccess (GrantedAccess & CallTrace)*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon#event-id-10-processaccess
  - Microsoft Learn — *Configuring Additional LSA Protection (RunAsPPL) & MiniDumpWriteDump API*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/security/credentials-protection-and-management/configuring-additional-lsa-protection
  - Splunk SURGe & LOLBAS Project — *Detecting LSASS Credential Dumping via comsvcs.dll (MiniDump / Ordinal #24)*: https://lolbas-project.github.io/lolbas/Libraries/Comsvcs/

## 7. Active Directory Kerberoasting & Pass-the-Hash Lateral Movement
- **Scenario ID:** `ad-kerberoasting`
- **Code:** T1558.003
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/ad-kerberoasting
- **Category:** Active Directory & Identity (`ACTIVE_DIRECTORY`)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1558.003 (Kerberoasting), T1550.002 (Pass the Hash), T1543.003 (Windows Service)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2022-33679, CVE-2021-42287 / CVE-2021-42278
- **Executive Summary:** Standard domain user `CORP\j.miller` on `WKS-OPS-12` (`10.20.14.44`) queries LDAP TCP/389 on `CORP-DC01` for user objects with a `servicePrincipalName` (`MSSQLSvc/FIN-SQL01.corp.local:1433` -> `svc_sql_prod`), requests a Kerberos TGS service ticket advertising legacy RC4-HMAC (`TicketEncryptionType 0x17`, logged in Security `EID 4769`), cracks `$krb5tgs$23$` offline via Hashcat `-m 13100` with zero account lockouts, and pivots laterally into `FIN-SQL01` via Pass-the-Hash (`EID 4624` LogonType 3 NTLM) + remote service installation (`EID 7045`). Defenders catch `EID 4769 (0x17)` for non-`$` service accounts and harden via AES-256 (`0x12`) + 120-char auto-rotated gMSAs.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1558.003] ACTIVE DIRECTORY LDAP SPN DISCOVERY BY STANDARD DOMAIN USER**: Unprivileged LDAP search returns `svc_sql_prod` (`MSSQLSvc/FIN-SQL01.corp.local:1433`).
  2. **[T1558.003] KERBEROS TGS SERVICE TICKET REQUEST WITH RC4-HMAC DOWNGRADE (0x17)**: `CORP-DC01` seals the TGS ticket with `svc_sql_prod` NTLM hash and logs Security `EID 4769` (`TicketEncryptionType 0x17`).
  3. **[T1558.003] OFFLINE GPU CRACKING VIA HASHCAT MODE 13100**: External GPU rig recovers `svc_sql_prod` credentials with zero Active Directory failed-logon (`EID 4625`) alerts.
  4. **[T1550.002] PASS-THE-HASH LATERAL MOVEMENT TO FIN-SQL01 & AES-256 GMSA DEFENSE**: NTLM LogonType 3 (`EID 4624`) + `SqlHealthDiag` service (`EID 7045`) on `FIN-SQL01`, remediated with AES-256 (`0x12`) + gMSAs.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - MITRE ATT&CK — *T1558.003 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting*: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1558/003/
  - Microsoft Security Auditing — *Event ID 4769: A Kerberos service ticket was requested*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4769
  - CISA & NSA — *Detecting and Mitigating Active Directory Compromises*: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories

## 8. Zerologon — Netlogon AES-CFB8 Zero-IV Authentication Bypass & DC Machine Account Reset
- **Scenario ID:** `zerologon-netlogon-cve-2020-1472`
- **Code:** CVE-2020-1472
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/zerologon-netlogon-cve-2020-1472
- **Category:** Active Directory & Identity (`ACTIVE_DIRECTORY`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1210 (Exploitation of Remote Services), T1098 (Account Manipulation), T1003.006 (DCSync)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2020-1472 (CVSS 10.0 CRITICAL), CISA ED 20-04
- **Executive Summary:** An unauthenticated host (`10.20.40.92`) reaches `CORP-DC01` over MS-NRPC (`NetrServerReqChallenge` + `NetrServerAuthenticate3` with `NegotiateFlags = 0x212FFFFF`, disabling Secure RPC) and sends ~256 all-zero 8-byte challenges exploiting Netlogon's `ComputeNetlogonCredential` AES-CFB8 flaw with a hardcoded 16-byte all-zero IV (`1/256` collision probability). Once authenticated as `CORP-DC01$`, the attacker calls `NetrServerPasswordSet2` with an empty 516-byte buffer to blank the Domain Controller machine password (`EID 4742`, Netlogon `EID 5823/5827`) and immediately executes DCSync (`EID 4662`), stopped permanently by Microsoft KB4557222 `FullSecureChannelProtection = 1`.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1210] UNAUTHENTICATED MS-NRPC PROBING WITH ALL-ZERO CHALLENGES**: ~256 rapid `NetrServerReqChallenge` / `NetrServerAuthenticate3` calls without Secure RPC (`0x212FFFFF`).
  2. **[T1210] AES-CFB8 ZERO-IV COLLISION & MACHINE IDENTITY IMPERSONATION**: 1-in-256 all-zero ciphertext collision grants `CORP-DC01$` Netlogon session authentication.
  3. **[T1098] NETRSERVERPASSWORDSET2 EMPTY DC MACHINE PASSWORD RESET**: `CORP-DC01$` machine hash reset to blank (`Security EID 4742`, Netlogon `EID 5823/5827`).
  4. **[T1003.006] IMMEDIATE DCSYNC EXTRACTION & KB4557222 SECURE RPC HARDENING**: Empty machine credential abused for `IDL_DRSGetNCChanges` (`EID 4662`), remediated via `FullSecureChannelProtection = 1`.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Secura BV (Tom Tervoort) — *Zerologon: Unauthenticated Domain Controller Compromise (CVE-2020-1472)*: https://www.secura.com/blog/zero-logon
  - Microsoft MSRC & Support — *CVE-2020-1472 Netlogon Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability (KB4557222)*: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/topic/how-to-manage-the-changes-in-netlogon-secure-channel-connections-associated-with-cve-2020-1472-f7e8cc17-0309-1d6a-304e-5ba73cd1a11e
  - CISA Emergency Directive 20-04 — *Mitigate Netlogon Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability*: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/directives/ed-20-04-mitigate-netlogon-elevation-privilege-vulnerability-august-2020-patch-tuesday

## 9. Active Directory DCSync — Rogue MS-DRSR DRSUAPI Replication & Event ID 4662
- **Scenario ID:** `dfir-dcsync-drsuapi-replication-eid4662`
- **Code:** T1003.006
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/dfir-dcsync-drsuapi-replication-eid4662
- **Category:** Active Directory & Identity (`ACTIVE_DIRECTORY`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1003.006 (OS Credential Dumping: DCSync), T1078.002 (Domain Accounts)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** MITRE T1003.006 / MS-DRSR Directory Replication Service Protocol
- **Executive Summary:** Operating from non-Domain-Controller workstation `WKS-FIN-09` (`10.20.40.118`), a compromised identity holding delegated Active Directory replication ACEs (`DS-Replication-Get-Changes` `1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2` and `DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All` `1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2`) binds to `CORP-DC01` over MS-DRSR (`drsuapi`, `IDL_DRSBind` -> `IDL_DRSGetNCChanges` Opnum 3) and replicates `krbtgt` and `Administrator` password hashes straight out of `NTDS.dit` without touching `lsass.exe` on the DC. Defenders detect DCSync via Domain Controller Security `EID 4662` matching the replication GUIDs from non-DC computer accounts and Zeek DCE/RPC `drsuapi` monitoring.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1078.002] DELEGATED REPLICATION ACL DISCOVERY ON DOMAIN ROOT**: Enumeration reveals `DS-Replication-Get-Changes` (`1131f6aa-...`) and `Get-Changes-All` (`1131f6ad-...`) on a non-DC account.
  2. **[T1003.006] ROGUE MS-DRSR IDL_DRSBIND FROM NON-DC WORKSTATION**: Workstation `10.20.40.118` opens an RPC `drsuapi` replication channel against `CORP-DC01`.
  3. **[T1003.006] IDL_DRSGETNCCHANGES (OPNUM 3) KRBTGT HASH EXTRACTION**: Directory Replication Service streams `krbtgt` and `Administrator` hashes while emitting `EID 4662` with both replication GUIDs.
  4. **[T1003.006] EID 4662 CORRELATION, ACL REVOCATION & KRBTGT DOUBLE-RESET**: SIEM correlates non-DC `EID 4662` + Zeek `drsuapi`, revokes rogue ACLs, and executes double `krbtgt` password reset.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - MITRE ATT&CK — *T1003.006 OS Credential Dumping: DCSync*: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/006/
  - Microsoft Open Specifications — *MS-DRSR Directory Replication Service (DRS) Remote Protocol (IDL_DRSGetNCChanges)*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-drsr/f977faaa-673e-4f66-b9bf-48c640241d47
  - Microsoft Security Auditing — *Event ID 4662: An operation was performed on an object*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/threat-protection/auditing/event-4662

## 10. Apache Log4Shell — JNDI Lookup Injection, Rogue LDAP Class Loading & RCE
- **Scenario ID:** `log4shell-dfir`
- **Code:** CVE-2021-44228
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/log4shell-dfir
- **Category:** Network & C2 Exfiltration (`NETWORK_WEB`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application), T1203 (Exploitation for Client Execution), T1105 (Ingress Tool Transfer)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2021-44228 (CVSS 10.0 CRITICAL), CVE-2021-45046
- **Executive Summary:** An external HTTP request carrying a JNDI lookup expression inside the `User-Agent` header reaches `APP-WEB-01` running Apache `log4j-core 2.14.1`. When Log4j formats the untrusted header, `JndiLookup` evaluates the expression and forces the Java server to connect outbound over LDAP TCP/1389 to rogue directory `198.51.100.77`, retrieve a remote Java class reference (`javaCodeBase` / `javaFactory`), and spawn `/bin/sh` child processes under `java.exe` (`Sysmon EID 1/3`, Suricata JNDI signature). Defenders patch to Log4j `2.17.1+`, enforce outbound LDAP/RMI egress blocks, and hunt `java` spawning shell interpreters.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1190] UNTRUSTED HTTP HEADER CONTAINING JNDI LOOKUP EXPRESSION**: Web request injects JNDI string into `User-Agent`, reaching Log4j `2.14.1` logger on `APP-WEB-01`.
  2. **[T1190] OUTBOUND JVM LDAP TCP/1389 LOOKUP TO ROGUE DIRECTORY**: `JndiManager` resolves the expression by connecting outbound to `198.51.100.77:1389` (`Sysmon EID 3`, Suricata alert).
  3. **[T1105] REMOTE CLASS REFERENCE FETCH & IN-JVM CLASS INITIALIZATION**: Rogue LDAP returns a `javaCodeBase` reference prompting class retrieval and execution inside the JVM (`java.exe`).
  4. **[T1203] JAVA CHILD SHELL EXECUTION, SIEM CORRELATION & LOG4J 2.17.1+ PATCH**: `java` spawns `/bin/sh` (`Sysmon EID 1` / `auditd`), contained via Log4j `2.17.1+` upgrade and egress LDAP/RMI blocks.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Apache Logging Services — *Apache Log4j Security Vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-44228 / CVE-2021-45046)*: https://logging.apache.org/log4j/2.x/security.html
  - CISA Advisory — *Apache Log4j Vulnerability Guidance (CVE-2021-44228)*: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/apache-log4j-vulnerability-guidance
  - MITRE ATT&CK — *T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application & T1105 Ingress Tool Transfer*: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/

## 11. DNS Tunneling Data Exfiltration & Covert TXT/A C2 Channel
- **Scenario ID:** `dns-tunneling-exfil`
- **Code:** T1071.004
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/dns-tunneling-exfil
- **Category:** Network & C2 Exfiltration (`NETWORK_WEB`)
- **Severity:** HIGH
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1071.004 (Application Layer Protocol: DNS), T1048.003 (Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** MITRE T1071.004 / T1048.003, SANS DNS Tunneling DFIR
- **Executive Summary:** Compromised workstation `WKS-DEV-19` (`10.20.14.55`) bypasses strict HTTP/HTTPS egress proxies by encoding `finance_q4.csv` into high-entropy hex/Base32 subdomain labels (`*.c2.exfil-lab.example`) sent over `UDP/53` through corporate recursive resolver `CORP-DNS01` (`Sysmon EID 22`, DNS Server Analytic `EID 256`). The attacker's authoritative nameserver reassembles each exfiltrated chunk and answers with base64-encoded C2 tasking inside `TXT` records. Defenders identify the covert channel via Shannon label entropy (> 3.8), extreme unique-subdomain-per-apex ratios, and DNS Response Policy Zone (RPZ) sinkholing.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1048.003] PAYLOAD CHUNKING & HIGH-ENTROPY HEX/BASE32 LABEL ENCODING**: Implant slices `finance_q4.csv` into <=63-byte DNS labels with Shannon entropy > 3.8 under `c2.exfil-lab.example`.
  2. **[T1071.004] RECURSIVE RESOLVER RELAY & SYSMON EID 22 BURST**: `CORP-DNS01` forwards hundreds of unique uncached `UDP/53` lookups, logging `Sysmon EID 22` and DNS `EID 256`.
  3. **[T1071.004] AUTHORITATIVE NAMESERVER REASSEMBLY & TXT RECORD C2 REPLY**: Rogue nameserver reconstructs stolen rows and returns Base64 tasking inside DNS `TXT` responses.
  4. **[T1071.004] SHANNON ENTROPY ANALYTICS & DNS RPZ SINKHOLE CONTAINMENT**: SIEM flags anomalous unique-label volume and `TXT` response sizes, blocking `c2.exfil-lab.example` via RPZ sinkhole.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - MITRE ATT&CK — *T1071.004 Application Layer Protocol: DNS & T1048.003 Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol*: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/
  - SANS Institute — *Detecting DNS Tunneling Through Entropy and Query Analytics*: https://www.sans.org/white-papers/34152/
  - Microsoft Sysinternals — *Sysmon Event ID 22: DNSEvent (DNS Query)*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sysinternals/downloads/sysmon#event-id-22-dnsevent-dns-query

## 12. AWS EC2 IMDSv1 SSRF Credential Theft & S3 Exfiltration
- **Scenario ID:** `aws-imdsv1-ssrf-capitalone-style`
- **Code:** T1552.005
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/aws-imdsv1-ssrf-capitalone-style
- **Category:** Cloud & SaaS (`CLOUD_SAAS`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application), T1552.005 (Unsecured Credentials: Cloud Instance Metadata API), T1530 (Data from Cloud Storage Object)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** AWS EC2 IMDSv2 Security Guidance, AWS GuardDuty InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS
- **Executive Summary:** External attacker exploits a misconfigured EC2 reverse proxy (`10.0.12.44`) via unvalidated SSRF to query link-local `169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/WAF-Role` over IMDSv1, harvests temporary STS `ASIA*` credentials, runs bulk `aws s3 sync` from an external IP (`CloudTrail ListBuckets`/`GetObject`, `GuardDuty UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS`), and contrasts unauthenticated IMDSv1 against IMDSv2 session tokens (`HttpTokens=required`, `HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1`).
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1190] MISCONFIGURED REVERSE-PROXY SSRF TO LINK-LOCAL METADATA**: External crafted request forces the EC2 WAF reverse proxy to relay a plain HTTP GET to `169.254.169.254`.
  2. **[T1552.005] IMDSV1 ROLE QUERY & TEMPORARY STS KEY THEFT**: IMDSv1 returns `WAF-Role` `AccessKeyId (ASIA*)`, `SecretAccessKey`, and `Token` without requiring a PUT session token.
  3. **[T1530] EXTERNAL S3 BUCKET ENUMERATION & BULK EXFILTRATION**: Attacker exports stolen STS keys externally and runs `aws s3 sync`, generating CloudTrail `ListBuckets`/`GetObject` bursts and GuardDuty `InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS`.
  4. **[T1552.005] IMDSV2 SESSION TOKEN ENFORCEMENT & LEAST-PRIVILEGE HARDENING**: Enforcing `HttpTokens=required` and `HttpPutResponseHopLimit=1` blocks SSRF relay while scoped IAM policies prevent cross-bucket S3 sync.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Amazon Web Services — *Use IMDSv2 on Amazon EC2 Instances*: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-instance-metadata-service.html
  - AWS GuardDuty — *UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration.OutsideAWS*: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/guardduty/latest/ug/guardduty_finding-types-iam.html
  - MITRE ATT&CK — *T1552.005 Cloud Instance Metadata API*: https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/005/

## 13. SolarWinds SUNSPOT Build Hijack & SUNBURST Supply-Chain Backdoor
- **Scenario ID:** `solarwinds-sunburst-orion-supply-chain`
- **Code:** T1195.002
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/solarwinds-sunburst-orion-supply-chain
- **Category:** Supply Chain & CI/CD (`SUPPLY_CHAIN_CICD`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1195.002 (Compromise Software Supply Chain), T1553.002 (Code Signing), T1568.002 (Domain Generation Algorithms), T1552.004 (Private Keys: AD FS Golden SAML)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CISA Emergency Directive 21-01 / Advisory AA20-352A, CrowdStrike SUNSPOT, Mandiant SUNBURST
- **Executive Summary:** `SUNSPOT` watches `MsBuild.exe` on the SolarWinds Orion build server to silently swap `InventoryManager.cs` before legitimate Authenticode signing of `SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll`, ships the trojanized update to thousands of enterprises, sleeps 12–14 days before issuing DGA DNS queries to `*.appsync-api.*.avsvmcloud[.]com`, and pivots via TEARDROP memory loading and AD FS token-signing certificate theft (`Golden SAML`).
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1195.002] SUNSPOT BUILD-SERVER WATCHER & INVENTORYMANAGER.CS SWAP**: `SUNSPOT` intercepts `MsBuild.exe` compiling `Orion.Core.BusinessLayer` and injects `OrionImprovementBusinessLayer` source code pre-build.
  2. **[T1553.002] LEGITIMATE AUTHENTICODE SIGNING & TROJANIZED UPDATE DISTRIBUTION**: Build pipeline signs the backdoored DLL with SolarWinds' authentic certificate and publishes it to customer update portals.
  3. **[T1568.002] 12-TO-14-DAY DORMANCY & AVSVMCLOUD DGA DNS BEACONING**: Implant checks uptime/security-tool blocklists, encodes victim domain identity into `avsvmcloud[.]com` CNAME queries, and awaits activation.
  4. **[T1552.004] TEARDROP STAGING, AD FS GOLDEN SAML & REPRODUCIBLE BUILD AUDIT**: Operators stage TEARDROP in memory, export the AD FS token-signing key for Golden SAML cloud access, and are countered via reproducible builds and DNS/AD FS telemetry.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - CrowdStrike Intelligence — *SUNSPOT: An Implant in the Build Process*: https://www.crowdstrike.com/blog/sunspot-malware-technical-analysis/
  - Mandiant — *SolarWinds SUNBURST Backdoor Technical Analysis*: https://cloud.google.com/blog/topics/threat-intelligence/evasive-attacker-leverages-solarwinds-supply-chain-compromises-with-sunburst-backdoor/
  - CISA — *Alert AA20-352A SolarWinds Orion Compromise*: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa20-352a

## 14. AuKill BYOVD EDR Killer via Signed Process Explorer Driver
- **Scenario ID:** `aukill-edr-killer-procxp152-byovd`
- **Code:** T1543.003
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/aukill-edr-killer-procxp152-byovd
- **Category:** Kernel, Firmware & BYOVD (`KERNEL_FIRMWARE_BYOVD`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1543.003 (Windows Service), T1068 (Exploitation for Privilege Escalation), T1562.001 (Disable or Modify Tools), T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** Sophos X-Ops AuKill BYOVD Analysis, LOLDrivers PROCEXP152.sys, Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist
- **Executive Summary:** Ransomware operators drop an outdated Microsoft-signed Sysinternals Process Explorer driver (`PROCEXP152.sys`), register it via Service Control Manager (`Event ID 7045` / `Sysmon EID 6`), send `DeviceIoControl` IOCTLs (`0x8335003C` / `0x83350004`) to open Ring 0 `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS` handles across Protected Process Light (PPL) boundaries, terminate EDR sensors in a continuous loop before encryption, and are blocked by Windows HVCI and Microsoft Vulnerable Driver Blocklist rules.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1543.003] SIGNED PROCEXP152.SYS DROP & SCM KERNEL SERVICE LOAD**: Operator writes `PROCEXP152.sys` and loads it into Ring 0, emitting Windows `Event ID 7045` and `Sysmon EID 6`.
  2. **[T1068] DEVICEIOCONTROL RING 0 HANDLE ESCALATION ACROSS PPL**: AuKill opens `\\.\PROCEXP152` and invokes IOCTL `0x8335003C` to acquire `PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS` handles to PPL-protected EDR processes.
  3. **[T1562.001] CONTINUOUS EDR TERMINATION LOOP**: User-mode loop kills `MsMpEng.exe` and `CSFalconService.exe` repeatedly via kernel-granted handles so services cannot respawn.
  4. **[T1486] UNCONTESTED RANSOMWARE LAUNCH VS. HVCI & DRIVER BLOCKLIST**: With EDR blinded, ransomware stages freely unless HVCI and Microsoft Recommended Driver Block Rules deny `PROCEXP152.sys` at load time.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Sophos X-Ops — *AuKill EDR Killer Abuses Process Explorer Driver*: https://news.sophos.com/en-us/2023/04/19/aukill-edr-killer-malware-abuses-process-explorer-driver/
  - LOLDrivers Project — *Vulnerable Signed Drivers Catalog*: https://www.loldrivers.io/
  - Microsoft Learn — *Microsoft Recommended Driver Block Rules & HVCI*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/application-security/application-control/app-control-for-business/design/microsoft-recommended-driver-block-rules

## 15. runc Leaky Vessels Container Escape via Leaked Host File Descriptor (CVE-2024-21626)
- **Scenario ID:** `runc-leaky-vessels-cwd-fd-escape-cve-2024-21626`
- **Code:** CVE-2024-21626
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/runc-leaky-vessels-cwd-fd-escape-cve-2024-21626
- **Category:** Containers, Kubernetes & Mesh (`CONTAINERS_KUBERNETES`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1611 (Escape to Host), T1552.001 (Credentials In Files)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2024-21626 (CVSS 8.6 HIGH, CISA KEV), GHSA-xr7r-f8xq-vfvv, Snyk Leaky Vessels
- **Executive Summary:** In `runc < 1.1.12`, an internal `/sys/fs/cgroup` host file descriptor opened during container initialization lacks `O_CLOEXEC` and leaks into the container process. Configuring an OCI image `WORKDIR /proc/self/fd/7` or running `runc exec --cwd /proc/self/fd/7` places the process working directory outside the container rootfs on the host mount namespace, enabling `../../../../etc/shadow` credential reads and host root escape until patched in `runc 1.1.12+` and monitored via `auditd` and Falco.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1611] UNCLOSED HOST CGROUP FILE DESCRIPTOR IN RUNC INIT**: `runc init` opens host `/sys/fs/cgroup` without `O_CLOEXEC`, leaving file descriptor `7` live across container spawn.
  2. **[T1611] WORKDIR /PROC/SELF/FD/7 ESCAPES MOUNT NAMESPACE**: Malicious OCI `WORKDIR` or `runc exec --cwd` resolves `/proc/self/fd/7` to the host cgroup directory outside the container rootfs.
  3. **[T1552.001] RELATIVE HOST FILESYSTEM TRAVERSAL & /ETC/SHADOW READ**: Container process traverses `../../../../etc/shadow` and writes host cron/SSH persistence across the host filesystem.
  4. **[T1611] RUNC 1.1.12 O_CLOEXEC PATCH & FALCO / AUDITD RUNTIME DETECTION**: Patched `runc` enforces `O_CLOEXEC` and post-`chdir` rootfs verification while Falco alerts on `/proc/self/fd` `cwd` anomalies.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - OpenContainers — *GHSA-xr7r-f8xq-vfvv runc CVE-2024-21626 Advisory*: https://github.com/opencontainers/runc/security/advisories/GHSA-xr7r-f8xq-vfvv
  - Snyk Security Labs — *Leaky Vessels CVE-2024-21626 Technical Analysis*: https://snyk.io/blog/cve-2024-21626-runc-process-cwd-container-breakout/
  - NIST NVD — *CVE-2024-21626 Detail*: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-21626

## 16. AI RAG Indirect Prompt Injection & MCP Tool Exfiltration Audit
- **Scenario ID:** `ai-rag-indirect-prompt-injection-mcp-tool-audit`
- **Code:** OWASP-LLM01
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/ai-rag-indirect-prompt-injection-mcp-tool-audit
- **Category:** AI, LLM Agents & MLOps Security (`AI_LLM_MLOPS_SECURITY`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application), T1059 (Command and Scripting Interpreter), T1041 (Exfiltration Over C2 Channel)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** OWASP LLM01:2025 & LLM06, MITRE ATLAS AML.T0051.001, NIST AI 100-2 E2025
- **Executive Summary:** An adversary plants hidden directive instructions inside an untrusted vendor document indexed in an enterprise RAG vector store. When an employee asks the AI assistant to summarize vendor records, the poisoned chunk is concatenated directly into the LLM prompt context window, tricking the model into calling privileged Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools (`read_internal_secrets` + `send_external_webhook`) to exfiltrate confidential enterprise records until contained by structured instruction-data separation, least-privilege MCP schemas, and human-in-the-loop approval gates.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1190] POISONED UNTRUSTED DOCUMENT INGESTED INTO RAG VECTOR STORE**: Hidden adversarial directive text is embedded inside a routine external document and indexed alongside clean enterprise records.
  2. **[T1059] SEMANTIC RETRIEVAL & PRIVILEGED PROMPT CONTEXT CONCATENATION**: Employee query triggers top-k vector retrieval, concatenating untrusted chunk directives directly alongside trusted system instructions.
  3. **[T1041] CONFUSED-DEPUTY MCP TOOL INVOCATION & WEBHOOK EXFILTRATION**: Hijacked agent invokes `read_internal_secrets` and `send_external_webhook`, streaming sensitive enterprise records externally while logging MCP tool audit telemetry.
  4. **[T1059] INSTRUCTION-DATA SEPARATION, LEAST-PRIVILEGE MCP & HUMAN APPROVAL GATES**: Guarded pipeline isolates retrieved data blocks, enforces strict egress allowlists, and requires explicit human approval for high-impact MCP tool calls.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - OWASP GenAI Security Project — *LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection*: https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/
  - MITRE ATLAS — *AML.T0051.001 Indirect LLM Prompt Injection*: https://atlas.mitre.org/techniques/AML.T0051.001
  - NIST — *NIST AI 100-2 E2025 Adversarial Machine Learning*: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ai/100/2/e2025/final

## 17. WannaCry Ransomware Worm — EternalBlue MS17-010 SMBv1 Exploit, Kill-Switch & .WNCRY Encryption
- **Scenario ID:** `wannacry-eternalblue-smb-worm-cve-2017-0144`
- **Code:** CVE-2017-0144
- **Canonical URL:** https://www.attackexplorer.com/scenarios/wannacry-eternalblue-smb-worm-cve-2017-0144
- **Category:** Ransomware & Extortion (`RANSOMWARE_EXTORTION`)
- **Severity:** CRITICAL
- **MITRE ATT&CK Techniques:** T1210 (Exploitation of Remote Services), T1497.001 (Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion: System Checks), T1486 (Data Encrypted for Impact), T1490 (Inhibit System Recovery)
- **CVEs / Advisories:** CVE-2017-0144 (CVSS 9.8 CRITICAL, MS17-010), CVE-2017-0145, CISA Alert TA17-132A
- **Executive Summary:** On unpatched Windows hosts exposing legacy SMBv1 (`TCP/445`), an infected peer delivers EternalBlue (`CVE-2017-0144` / `MS17-010`), exploiting a 32-bit-to-16-bit FEA length truncation inside `srv.sys!SrvOs2FeaListSizeToNt` to overflow the non-paged kernel pool (`0xFFFFFA8004C21000`), corrupt adjacent `SRVNET_BUFFER_HDR` pointers, implant the DoublePulsar Ring 0 backdoor (`Multiplex ID 0x0052`), and execute `mssecsvc.exe` (`PID 3412`) without credentials. Before detonating, `mssecsvc.exe` performs an unauthenticated WinINet HTTP check against hardcoded unregistered domain `iuqerfsodp9ifjaposdfjhgosurijfaewrwergwea.com`; receiving `NXDOMAIN`, it installs service `mssecsvc2.0`, unpacks `tasksche.exe` (`WNcRY@2ol7`), encrypts 176 extensions with unique per-file `AES-128-CBC` keys wrapped in `RSA-2048` (`WANACRY!` / `.WNCRY`), wipes Volume Shadow Copies (`vssadmin` / `wbadmin` / `bcdedit`), and sprays 128 scanner threads across `/24` LANs and random WAN IPs until Marcus Hutchins registers the kill-switch sinkhole (`HTTP 200 OK` -> `ExitProcess(0)`) and defenders apply `MS17-010` and disable SMBv1.
- **Kill-Chain Stages (4):**
  1. **[T1210] ETERNALBLUE SMBV1 KERNEL POOL OVERFLOW & DOUBLEPULSAR RING 0 IMPLANT**: Crafted SMBv1 `Trans2` FEA packets trigger `srv.sys!SrvOs2FeaListSizeToNt` non-paged pool overflow over TCP/445, corrupting `SRVNET_BUFFER_HDR` and installing DoublePulsar (`0x0052`) to inject `mssecsvc.exe`.
  2. **[T1497.001] HARDCODED WININET KILL-SWITCH DOMAIN PROBE (NXDOMAIN GATE)**: `mssecsvc.exe` calls `InternetOpenUrlA` on `http://iuqerfsodp9ifjaposdfjhgosurijfaewrwergwea.com`; `NXDOMAIN` confirms a live network and authorizes service install (`mssecsvc2.0`, `EID 7045`).
  3. **[T1486] TASKSCHE.EXE HYBRID AES-128 + RSA-2048 .WNCRY ENCRYPTION & SHADOW WIPE**: `tasksche.exe` unpacks resource archive `WNcRY@2ol7`, encrypts 176 file extensions with `WANACRY!` headers (`.WNCRY`), drops `@WanaDecryptor@.exe`, and wipes shadow copies (`vssadmin` / `wbadmin` / `bcdedit`).
  4. **[T1490] 128-THREAD TCP/445 WORM PROPAGATION, KILL-SWITCH SINKHOLE & MS17-010 PATCH**: Parallel LAN/WAN EternalBlue scanning is halted globally when sinkhole registration returns `HTTP 200 OK` (`ExitProcess(0)`), reinforced permanently by `MS17-010`, SMBv1 disablement, and VLAN TCP/445 segmentation.
- **Primary Authoritative Sources (3):**
  - Microsoft Security Response Center — *Microsoft Security Bulletin MS17-010 (CVE-2017-0144)*: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/security-updates/securitybulletins/2017/ms17-010
  - CISA / US-CERT — *Alert TA17-132A: Indicators Associated With WannaCry Ransomware*: https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2017/05/12/indicators-associated-wannacry-ransomware
  - MITRE ATT&CK — *Software S0366: WannaCry*: https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0366/
